newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron settler warns of explosion in redeployment.
newsitem.headline: Hebron settler warns of explosion in redeployment.

text.p: A leader of the outlawed Jewish extremist Kach movement warned in remarks broadcast on Saturday of an explosion if an Israeli troop redeployment were carried out in the West Bank town of Hebron.

"There are certain groups, particularly in Kiryat Arba, that are organising initiated operations and I have been invited lately to gatherings very frequently (on this)," Baruch Merzel, who is one of some 400 Jewish settlers living amidst 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron, told Israel Radio.

Kiryat Arba Jewish settlement adjacent to Hebron is home to 5,500 Israelis. One of them, Baruch Goldstein, shot dead 29 Palestinians at prayer in Hebron's al-Ibrahimi mosque in February, 1994, before he was killed by survivors.
The anti-Arab Kach movement was outlawed after the massacre.
"I've warned in the past and I'm warning today that the territory is on the verge of explosion. I know that they're talking about practical organisation," Merzel said.
Merzel said there were plans to run settler patrols, to enter Arab neighbourhoods and "all sorts of things".

"Kiryat Arba, Hebron are not Gush Katif and Psagot. These are other people...We have a record of reaction to Arab provocations. We will not go like a herd of sheep to slaughter even if the government is a rightwing government," he said.

Gush Katif is the Jewish settlement area still under Israeli control in the Gaza Strip most of which Israel handed to Palestinian rule in 1994. Psagot is a Jewish settlement in the West Bank adjacent to Ramallah self-rule enclave.
Israel and the Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) began negotiations this week on implementing a deal signed by Israel's previous government with the PLO to redeploy Israeli troops in Hebron.

Palestinians doubt rightwing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu intends to uphold the existing agreement. They say he wants to rewrite it. Netanyahu says he must increase security provisions for settlers in Hebron.
